basics.name: Oscar Jaroker
basics.summary: I am a senior at Colgate University studying Applied Mathematics and Physics, with an interest in mathematical modeling, data analysis, and the computational methods behind simulation and optimization. My experience spans high performance computing in C, statistical modeling in R and Python, embedded sensing with Arduino, and quantitative work in corporate finance.

education.area: Applied Mathematics and Physics Double Major with Coursework in Computer Science

work.name: National Security Agency
work.summary: High performance data movement for large-scale compute systems
highlights: Co-developed a multithreaded C file-transfer utility slated to replace the incumbent HPC transfer tool, outperforming every alternative benchmarked; raised sustained throughput over a 200 Gbit/s InfiniBand fabric by 29% over the incumbent on RAM-backed storage and 32% on a Lustre parallel filesystem

Designed the tool's shipped congestion-control algorithm, keyed on delivery rate and minimum RTT rather than packet loss: 260% higher throughput than TCP CUBIC on a lossy emulated WAN and 74% lower transfer time on high-bandwidth-delay paths, eliminating a throughput-collapse failure mode

Delivered weekly progress presentations to interns and staff; co-authored the project's technical paper and a second paper documenting the team's AI-assisted software engineering workflow, for use as an internal resource

projects.name: Koopman Analysis of Chua's Circuit
projects.summary: Final Project for Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
highlights: Built Chua's Circuit in lab and collected time-series data across four dynamical regimes: fixed point, limit cycle, period-doubled, and double scroll
Applied Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) to approximate the Koopman operator and extract dominant frequencies and geometric structure from each regime
Characterized the chaotic double scroll attractor via Lyapunov exponent estimation, correlation dimension, and box-counting dimension

projects.name: glmOJ: Count Regression R Package
projects.summary: Final Project for MATH 454 Statistical Learning
highlights: Developed an R package providing a unified workflow for fitting, diagnosing, and interpreting count and semi-continuous regression models
Supports Poisson, quasi-Poisson, negative binomial, Tweedie, and zero-inflated counterparts (ZIP, ZINB, ZI-Tweedie) with automatic model selection by AIC, BIC, log-likelihood, or McFadden pseudo-R²
Package site at oscar.jaroker.com/glmOJ

projects.name: Optimal Harvesting in Stochastic Predator-Prey Environment

Using MATLAB to implement numerical methods such as FB Sweep, Euler-Maruyama, Backward Euler

projects.name: Data Analysis of "Allentown": Measuring Musical Influence

Communicated results clearly in a written report, including visualizations and explanations
